sources_consulted.found: Confirmed Demon was censored; Junker/erotic poems circulated in manuscript, published 1879 Geneva anthology; explicitly excluded from Soviet complete collected works as unsuitable for print
State Public Historical Library (GPIB) catalog entry confirmed the 1879 Leipzig publication by E. L. Kasprovich; no English translation record present
The Demon and Other Poems, Eugene Kayden, 1965, Antioch Press — contains The Demon and other canonical poems; no erotic/forbidden content
The Demon, 1918, Douglas & Foulis, Edinburgh — only The Demon, no forbidden poems

Eros Russe: Russian Eros Not for Women (Lermontov), Berkeley Slavic Specialties, 3rd ed. 1995 — bilingual edition of Lermontov erotic poems; contents not confirmed, The Demon unlikely included given title and focus
Lermontov's junker poems (Hospital, Peterhof Holiday, Ulansha) described as never published for understandable reasons; no English translation mentioned
1875 English translation of The Demon by Alexander Condie Stephen confirmed to exist; page not accessible but title/date confirmed from multiple search results

reasoning: Leipzig 1879 compilation pairs The Demon (widely translated into English since 1875: Condie Stephen, Kayden 1965, Johnston, Pyman, Pettus et al.) with censored erotic Junker poems. No English of this complete compilation found. Forbidden/erotic poems excluded even from Soviet collected works; the 1995 Berkeley Slavic 'Eros Russe' may cover erotic poems but not alongside The Demon. First complete English of this compilation.
